verses.1: And when all the nations had crossed the Jordan, God said to Joshua, “Go.”
verses.2: Choose from the people twelve men, one man from each tribe.
verses.3: And he commanded them to say, “Take these stones from within the Jordan, from the place where the priests stood. There are twelve stones there. Carry them with you, and place them in the basket we have prepared for this purpose.”
verses.4: And Joshua called out to the twenty men who had been chosen from among the Israelites. One man after another was called upon to serve as a leader.
verses.5: And Joshua said to them, “Go ahead, go before the Lord your God. Go across the Jordan River. Then they will raise one stone for each of you, according to the number of families of the Israelites.”
verses.6: So that this will serve as a reminder for you, in case they ask you tomorrow, “What are these stones to you?”
verses.7: And you said to them, “Those stones were cut from the mountains in the Valley of Jehoshaphat. They were cut from the rocks in the Valley of Jehoshaphat. These stones will serve as a reminder for the children of Israel forever.”
verses.8: And so did the children of Israel, as Yehoshua commanded. They took twelve stones from the riverbed, just as Jehovah had told Yehoshua to do when counting the tribes of the children of Israel. They carried those stones with them and placed them in the ark.
verses.9: And twenty-one stones were built by Joshua within the Jordan River, under the feet of the priests who carried the Ark of the Covenant. These stones remained there until today.
verses.10: And the priests, who carried the Ark, stood in the middle of the Jordan until all that Jehovah had commanded Joshua to say to the people was completed. Then the people rushed forward and crossed over.
verses.11: And when all the people had gone away, then the Ark of God and the priests went before the people.
verses.12: And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad passed on, along with half of the tribe of Manasseh. They were fifty in number, before the children of Israel, as Moses commanded them.
verses.13: Four hundred thousand soldiers of the army went before Jehovah to fight against the enemies of Yericho.
verses.14: On that day, Jehovah made Yehoshua grow up in the eyes of all Israel. They saw him as they had seen Moses throughout his entire life.
verses.15: And the LORD said to Joshua, “Speak.”
verses.16: Command the priests to carry the utensils of the sanctuary, and let them ascend from the valley.
verses.17: And Joshua commanded the priests, “Go up from the Jordan.”
verses.18: And the priests, who were carrying the vessels of the covenant of Jehovah, went out from the Jordan River. Their feet were bound together, and they returned to their place in the Jordan River. Then they continued their journey along all its paths.
verses.19: And the people came up from the Jordan on the first day of the month. They camped at Gilgal, at the eastern end of Jericho.
verses.20: And these twelve stones, which were taken from the Valley of Jordan, were used by Joshua to build the altar.
verses.21: And he said to the children of Israel, “When you ask your fathers tomorrow, ‘What are these stones?’”
verses.22: And know that your children should say: In those days, Israel crossed the Jordan River.
verses.23: May the Lord your God cleanse the waters of the Jordan River from before you, just as He did for the Sea of Galilee. May He also cleanse those waters from before us until we cross over them.
verses.24: So that all the nations of the earth may know the power of the LORD, so that they may fear the LORD their God all days.
